hints.title: Pick a target letter for a window
hints.body: For a fixed substring, making it uniform means choosing the letter that already occurs most often and replacing every other character. The cost is `window length - maximum letter count`.

hints.title: Slide a window
hints.body: Extend the right end one character at a time. If the window's replacement cost exceeds `k`, move the left end forward until the cost is at most `k`. Track the largest valid window seen.

hints.title: Counts, not positions
hints.body: Keep an array of 26 counts for the current window. After adding a character, compute the largest count, then shrink while `length - largest > k`. Because the alphabet is fixed, finding the largest count costs only 26 operations.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
counts = 26 zeros
left = 0
best = 0
for right from 0 to length(s) - 1:
    counts[s[right]] += 1
    while (right - left + 1) - max(counts) > k:
        counts[s[left]] -= 1
        left += 1
    best = max(best, right - left + 1)
return best
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution. The `max(counts)` scan is constant work because the alphabet has 26 letters.
